t: The Secretary shall report the results of his investigation and study to Congress not later than December 31, 1967. Such report shall include but not be limited to (1) an inventory of existing capabilities, equipment, and facilities, either publicly or privately owned or operated, which could be made available for use by the Secretary in carrying out the safety research, development, and testing referred to in section 301, (2) recommendations as to the site or sites for any recommended facility or facilities, (3) preliminary plans, specifications, and drawings for such recommended facility or facilities (including major research, development, and testing equipment), and (4) the estimated cost of the recommended sites, facilities, and equipment.

fable.w: The section only requires the Secretary to report study results to Congress, which is inside the federal government. The mention of "publicly or privately owned" facilities is tempting, but it describes an inventory item in the report and not any consultation with outside parties. No comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue is created.
fable.s: The Secretary shall report the results of his investigation and study to Congress not later than December 31, 1967.

qwen_block.w: This section requires the Secretary to submit a report to Congress. Congress is part of the federal government, so this interaction is internal to the government and does not involve consultation or coordination with outside parties. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_block.s: The Secretary shall report the results of his investigation and study to Congress not later than December 31, 1967.

opus.w: The section only requires the Secretary to send a report to Congress, which is inside the federal government. Private facilities appear only as items in the report's inventory. No private party, state or member of the public is consulted, given a hearing or asked for comments before a federal decision, so this is not participation.
opus.s: The Secretary shall report the results of his investigation and study to Congress not later than December 31, 1967.
opus.b: Someone might read this as participation because the report must inventory "publicly or privately owned or operated" facilities, which brings in private parties. That reading fails. Private facilities are only things the report lists. Nobody outside the government is consulted, and the only action is a report to Congress, which is inside the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the Secretary to submit a report to Congress. Congress is an internal part of the federal government, so reporting to it is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside parties. The text does not mandate any consultation, hearings, or coordination with non-federal entities (such as the public, states, or experts) to generate the report.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall report the results of his investigation and study to Congress not later than December 31, 1967.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the report includes "recommendations as to the site or sites," this implies some form of consultation or participation in the decision-making process. However, the text only mandates a report *to* Congress. Congress is part of the federal government (inside the boundary), and reporting to an internal entity does not constitute participation with outside parties. Furthermore, the section does not describe *how* the Secretary gathers the information for the report (e.g., via public hearings or advisory committees); it only describes the output (the report). Therefore, there is no evidence of required or recommended participation with non-federal entities in this specific text.
